newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares steady, await new accounts.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares steady, await new accounts.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended flat on Monday on low turnover as the market remained in a state of limbo ahead of the introduction of trading accounts for foreign investors, brokers said.
"Banks should introduce first custodian account schemes later this week. Until then, shares may decline slightly while volumes will remain low," one broker said.
Four weeks ago the Bank of Slovenia said international investors would have to open a custodian account at a domestic bank in order to be able to trade in Slovenian securities.
So far none of the 14 fully licensed banks has said when it would be ready to start opening custodian accounts, but brokers believe an announcement is imminent.

"If banks announce they will be able to accept an inflow of at least half a million dollars per day through custodian accounts, this will be good news for market liquidity and shares will go up," the broker said.
The blue-chip SBI index firmed 0.51 points to 1,378.2.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded, closing unchanged at 56,000 tolars on volume of 310 shares.
Overall six shares rose, six fell, five were steady and nine were untraded. Turnover fell to 64.8 million tolars from 82.1 million on Friday.
Financial consultancy Dadas was the top gainer, surging 11.97 percent to 6,080 on volume of three shares.
The preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the leading decliners, tumbling 9.96 percent to 470 tolars on volume of 2,399 shares.
